title: Establishing credibility of FSI aortic valve leaflet models for coaptation and stress: a V&V 40-aligned, factor-by-factor assessment across mechanisms
runhead: FSI aortic valve leaflet credibility under V&V 40
device: Polymeric aortic valve leaflet with edge reinforcement, evaluated within a trileaflet assembly

models.name: Model A: ALE-based anisotropic shell FSI
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved leaflet deformation with contact-induced coaptation, coaptation area and line pressure, peak maximum principal stress and its location, and near-valvular flow kinematics

models.name: Model B: Immersed boundary FSI with homogenized leaflet material
models.what_it_computes: Effective orifice dynamics, surrogate regurgitant fraction from backflow waveform, cycle-averaged leaflet stress, and global pressure–flow characteristics

models.name: Model C: Partitioned FSI with compliant aortic root and mortar contact
models.what_it_computes: Coupled leaflet–root motion, closure-transient load amplification, spatial stress trajectories, and coaptation contact map over the cardiac cycle

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Diastolic coaptation under physiologic transvalvular pressure
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained seal quality determines regurgitation risk; inadequate coaptation area or line pressure compromises valve competence

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: Systolic opening at peak flow
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Peak leaflet stress in the open state governs durability and risk of material damage over repeated cycles

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 3: Rapid closure transient (water-hammer event)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High-rate loading during flow deceleration can trigger transient stress spikes and flutter onset, affecting acute safety and fatigue life

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored per model–mechanism pair on a 0–100 Credibility Index, with acceptance requiring every factor score ≥ 75 and no single score < 60 for any pair.

sections: Question of interest and context of use
Computational models: geometry, constitutive laws, coupling strategies, and computed quantities
Mechanisms and quantities of interest: coaptation metrics and stress metrics
Evidence plan and acceptance criteria on the 0–100 Credibility Index
Discretization error: mesh convergence protocols and element technology checks
Numerical solver error: partitioning tolerance, coupling stability, and time-integration accuracy
Model form: constitutive representation, contact/coaptation formulation, and fluid rheology choices
Model inputs: boundary conditions, material parameters, and uncertainties
Test conditions: hydrodynamic loop settings and physiologic waveform mapping
Test samples: leaflet constructs, mounting, and sample representativeness
Results: per-factor 0–100 scores for every model × mechanism pair, with coaptation and stress comparisons
Synthesis across mechanisms: weakest-link appraisal against acceptance criteria
Conclusion: Not accepted due to inadequate model form for the closure transient and unrepresentative test samples leading to failing Credibility Index scores in multiple model–mechanism pairs
